newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-ROMARIO RETURNS TO BRAZIL SQUAD AFTER TWO YEARS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ROMARIO RETURNS TO BRAZIL SQUAD AFTER TWO YEARS.

text.p: Striker Romario was included on Tuesday on the Brazil squad for next week's friendly international against Poland, the first time he has been picked by the national team for more than two years.
The tempestuous striker last played for his country in the World Cup final against Italy in July 1994. Since then he has been involved in a host of scandals and controversies on and off the field.

Coach Mario Zagallo, who took over after the World Cup, picked him for a friendly in late 1994 only to hear Romario say that he did not want to play international soccer until the Olympic Games in 1996.
A furious Zagallo had refused to pick Romario since, a punishment which shattered the striker's dream of playing in the Olympics.
In announcing his decision to give Romario another chance, Zagallo said: "Obviously, his behaviour has changed."
Romario, who has 19 goals in 38 full international appearances, said: "I felt like an 18-year-old player waiting to hear that he had been picked for the first time."
Romario, who turned 31 in January, was expected to partner Barcelona's Ronaldo on attack for the February 26 match in Goiania, some 150 kilometres from the capital of Brasilia.
He returned to Brazil to play for Rio de Janeiro club Flamengo in January 1995 only to find himself getting involved in a series of incidents off the beach.

Last July Romario was sold to Spanish club Valencia but returned to Flamengo less than three months later after falling out with coach Luis Aragones. This year, he has attempted, so far successfully, to build the image of a changed man.

He made a promising start to the 1997 Brazilian season, helping Flamengo reach the final of the pre-season Rio-Sao Paulo tournament and scoring four goals in two games in the Rio de Janeiro championship.
